title: A cursor that moves itself
hints: `*cursor` is the caller's `const char *`. Copy it into a local `const char *p = *cursor;`, move `p` along the text, and finish by writing it back with `*cursor = p;`.

Skip spaces while `*p == ' '`. If you then hit `'\0'`, there's no word: store the end position in `*cursor` and return false. Otherwise remember `start = p`, advance `p` until a space or `'\0'`, and fill `*word`, `*len` and `*cursor`.

`while (*p == ' ') p++; if (*p == '\0') { *cursor = p; return false; } const char *start = p; while (*p != '\0' && *p != ' ') p++; *word = start; *len = (size_t)(p - start); *cursor = p; return true;`
